overall: Atlanta is running warm at 13:05 ET with a running max of 89.6°F and an active warming velocity of +1.8°F/hr, suggesting the peak has not yet been reached. The high dewpoint of 69.8°F indicates a humid airmass, which can act as a modest cap on afternoon heating by reducing the efficiency of surface mixing. Light winds at 4.6 mph offer little convective relief or mixing to push temperatures higher.
forecast_obs_notes: Models are split into two camps: GFS and HRRR both target 92.1°F while ECMWF and NBM cluster at 90.0°F, a 2.1°F spread that reflects genuine uncertainty in afternoon boundary layer evolution. Observed temps are tracking well within the model envelope so far, but the hourly warming rate has been decelerating — from +2.7°F/hr between 09:00–11:00 down to roughly +0.9°F/hr between 11:00–13:00 — suggesting the upper model guidance may be a stretch.
max_temp_prediction: With ~2 hours of peak heating remaining (Atlanta typically peaks 15:00–16:00 ET), the running max of 89.6°F will almost certainly be exceeded, but the decelerating warming trend and humid airmass favor an outcome closer to the lower model camp near 90–91°F rather than the 92.1°F GFS/HRRR target. The ensemble signals are notably weak (both Tier 4 Avoid with ≤7% confidence at their respective tops), adding meaningful uncertainty and arguing against high-conviction bets above 91°F. Best estimate is approximately 91.0°F with moderate-low confidence.
